title: Inference & Serving
blurb: From a trained model to a useful product: how inference actually runs on a GPU, how to make it fast and cheap, how to call APIs, and the craft of writing the prompts that drive it.

nodes.label: The inference loop & KV cache
nodes.description: Prefill vs decode, what the KV cache stores, why prefill is FLOP-bound and decode is memory-bound. The mental model behind every serving choice.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why an LLM's first token is slower than the rest and why KV cache size dominates memory at long context.

resources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
resources.author: Kwon et al. (vLLM)
resources.annotation: The vLLM paper. The KV cache section is the clearest treatment of how cache memory dominates serving and what PagedAttention does about it.

resources.title: Transformer Inference Arithmetic
resources.author: Carol Chen (Kipply)
resources.annotation: Back-of-envelope math for inference latency, memory, and bandwidth. The post that makes 'memory-bound' viscerally clear.

resources.title: The LLM-Inference Math
resources.author: Pratik Bhavsar / Hugging Face
resources.annotation: Hugging Face's deep dive on the inference loop from the perspective of TGI. Pair with the vLLM paper for the two engines' framing.

resources.title: FlashAttention
resources.author: Dao et al.
resources.annotation: The reference implementation. FlashAttention-2 and -3 are the attention kernels that make modern inference KV-cache-bound rather than attention-bound.

nodes.label: Quantization (8-bit, 4-bit, GGUF, AWQ)
nodes.description: Why a 4-bit model fits in a quarter of the VRAM and still works. INT8, NF4, AWQ, GGUF formats; what each loses.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick a quantization scheme for a deployment target and predict its quality cost.

resources.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
resources.author: Frantar et al.
resources.annotation: GPTQ — the 4-bit recipe that put aggressive quantization in production. The math is approachable and grounds the practical choices.

resources.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
resources.author: Lin et al.
resources.annotation: AWQ. The pragmatic alternative to GPTQ; often higher quality at 4-bit and the default in many open-weights workflows.

resources.title: Hugging Face — Quantization
resources.annotation: The 'how do I actually do this' page. Covers bitsandbytes, GPTQ, AWQ, and HQQ with one-line APIs.

nodes.label: Batching strategies (continuous batching)
nodes.description: Static vs dynamic vs continuous batching. Why continuous batching is the single biggest throughput win in LLM serving.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe continuous batching and explain why vLLM and TGI default to it.

resources.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models
resources.author: Yu et al.
resources.annotation: The paper that introduced continuous (iteration-level) batching. The idea is in vLLM and TGI today.

resources.title: How continuous batching enables 23x throughput in LLM inference
resources.author: Anyscale
resources.annotation: The single best practitioner-level explainer. Diagrams, throughput plots, the why.

nodes.label: Speculative decoding
nodes.description: A small draft model proposes, a big target model verifies. The trick that gives most modern serving stacks their decode-time speedup.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain how speculative decoding preserves the target model's output distribution while running faster.

resources.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
resources.author: Leviathan, Kalman, Matias (Google)
resources.annotation: The canonical speculative-decoding paper. Eight pages; the rejection-sampling proof is the clean explanation of why outputs stay identical.

resources.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
resources.author: Cai et al.
resources.annotation: Medusa replaces the draft model with extra heads on the target. The pragmatic modern alternative; widely deployed.

nodes.label: Latency vs throughput trade-offs
nodes.description: Time-to-first-token, tokens-per-second, requests-per-second, the trade-off between user latency and aggregate throughput. The lens behind every serving decision.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick batching, model size, and precision to hit a stated latency-and-cost target.

resources.title: LLM Inference Performance Engineering: Best Practices
resources.author: Databricks Mosaic AI
resources.annotation: The clearest practical guide to the latency / throughput / cost surface. Read once; you'll know the right questions to ask.

resources.title: Transformer Inference Arithmetic
resources.author: Carol Chen (Kipply)
resources.annotation: Repeat reference because it's the right lens here too: latency and throughput both fall out of the inference arithmetic.

nodes.label: Serving engines (vLLM, TGI, SGLang, llama.cpp)
nodes.description: The open-source LLM serving stack. Each engine's sweet spot, when to reach for which, what they share in common.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick the right serving engine for a deployment scenario and justify it.

resources.title: vLLM
resources.annotation: The most-deployed open serving engine. Continuous batching + PagedAttention + a wide model zoo. The first one to try.

resources.title: Hugging Face Text Generation Inference (TGI)
resources.annotation: The Hugging Face serving engine. Production-grade, tight integration with the HF ecosystem.

resources.title: SGLang
resources.annotation: The engine optimized for complex agent + structured-output workloads. Fast prefix sharing and RadixAttention are the headline features.

resources.title: llama.cpp
resources.author: Georgi Gerganov
resources.annotation: The CPU / Apple-silicon / consumer-GPU serving engine. GGUF format, single-binary deploy. The right tool for laptop and edge.

nodes.label: Model APIs (closed and open)
nodes.description: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, the open-model APIs (Together, Groq, Fireworks). Streaming, tool use, structured output, caching, rate limits.
nodes.doneWhen: You're fluent in at least one closed-model API and one open-model API.

resources.title: Anthropic API documentation
resources.annotation: Streaming, tool use, prompt caching, batch, structured output. The reference for Claude; the patterns transfer to other providers.

resources.title: OpenAI API documentation
resources.annotation: The other half of the duopoly's reference. Functions, JSON mode, streaming, the Responses API.

resources.title: LiteLLM
resources.annotation: A unified OpenAI-shaped API across 100+ providers. The pragmatic answer when you want to swap models behind one client.

nodes.label: Structured output & constrained decoding
nodes.description: JSON-mode, function-calling schemas, grammar-constrained decoding, outlines / lm-format-enforcer. How you make an LLM produce a string your program can parse.
nodes.doneWhen: You can get reliable JSON out of a model and explain why constrained decoding outperforms 'please reply in JSON'.

resources.title: Outlines — Structured generation for LLMs
resources.annotation: Grammar / regex / JSON-schema constrained decoding. The reference open implementation; the README is a working tutorial.

resources.title: Anthropic — Tool use
resources.annotation: Function-call-shaped structured output, vendor-flavored. The cleanest reference for the closed-API approach.

resources.title: Instructor — structured outputs for LLMs
resources.annotation: Pydantic-typed responses from any LLM. The right tool when you want validated, typed dataclasses out of a model.

nodes.label: Prompt engineering as a craft
nodes.description: System prompts, few-shot, chain-of-thought, when to specify formats, when to give examples, when to break problems down. Treat it as engineering, not folklore.
nodes.doneWhen: You can systematically iterate on a prompt with measurements, not vibes.

resources.title: Prompt engineering overview — Anthropic
resources.annotation: The current best official guide. Be clear, use examples, structure with XML, chain-of-thought when helpful. The chapter on agentic systems is gold.

resources.title: Anthropic's Interactive Prompt Engineering Tutorial
resources.annotation: Nine chapters of working notebooks. The right way to learn the craft if you'd rather practice than read.

resources.title: Prompting Guide
resources.annotation: Vendor-neutral compendium of techniques. Use it as a reference for chain-of-thought / ReAct / self-consistency / TOT variants.

nodes.label: Inference cost engineering
nodes.description: Prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, smaller-model fallbacks, batching at the application layer. The difference between a system that scales economically and one that doesn't.
nodes.doneWhen: You can break down the dollar cost of an LLM feature and find the top three places to cut it.

resources.title: Prompt caching — Anthropic
resources.annotation: How provider-native prompt caching works and how to use it. The single highest-leverage cost lever for repeated-context workloads.

resources.title: Patterns for Building LLM-based Systems & Products
resources.author: Eugene Yan
resources.annotation: The single best-organized practitioner's survey of LLM-system patterns, including the section on caching and cost.
